proposed:
The same-pool open-model results differ: effort moved Qwen3-32B by **+0.172**
and gpt-oss-120b by **+0.015**, against **−0.007** for Opus. In this comparison,
additional reasoning closes part of the discrimination gap for Qwen3-32B,
changes gpt-oss-120b only slightly and does not improve Opus. Opus reaches its
approximately 0.95 AUC at low effort rather than reasoning its way there at
maximum effort. Practically, the screen can use about **4× fewer reasoning
tokens (~2× all-in)** with no detectable loss. That saving appears in the run
logs but is not recorded in the committed AUC artifacts.[^s-effort]
rationale: The current text generalizes from three models to weak and strong detectors and describes low-effort classification as recognition “at a glance.” The rewrite confines interpretation to the measured systems, preserves every effect and cost figure, and matches “no loss” to the experiment's resolution.
